title: Emile, or On Education
author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
current_text: On 9 June 1762, the Parlement de Paris condemned Emile, or On Education to be torn and burned and ordered the arrest of its author; the author narrowly escaped arrest when the judgment was executed on 11 June. The government of Geneva also condemned Emile, or On Education. Emile, or On Education was banned in Paris and Geneva because of its section titled “Profession of Faith of the Savoyard Vicar.” Emile, or On Education was forbidden by the Church and listed on the Index Librorum Prohibitorum.

sources.quote:
Emile, or On Education (French: Émile, ou De l'éducation), first published in 1762, is a treatise on the nature of education and on the nature of man written by Jean-Jacques Rousseau, who considered it to be the "best and most important" of all his writings.
Due to a section of the book titled "Profession of Faith of the Savoyard Vicar", Emile was banned in Paris and Geneva and was publicly burned in the first year of its publication.
